Issued at 306 AM EDT Sat Sep 12 2026

PATTERN SYNOPSIS/FORECAST:

Zonal flow across the western US attm...with ridge axis holding on 
across the eastern US, including the Great Lakes. Flow remains a bit 
split attm...with a beautiful swirl in water vapor imagery over the 
Mid MS Valley associated with a trough axis there...and an elongated 
positively tilted trough axis stretching from the northern Plains to 
an upper low over Hudson Bay, with many-a PV maxima in the flow 
across most of Canada attm. Deepest moisture remains across the SE 
US and Lower MS Valley nearer that former feature...with a maximum 
in pwats (around 2in) along the tightening baroclinic zone and 
deformation axis stretching from central Ontario back into 
Nebraska...though there is a little bit of moisture hanging back 
across central Canada along a subtle trough axis, near and north of 
which 850mb temps drop back to 0-4C. Plume of weak stability also 
stretches along the aforementioned baroclinic zone, and this is 
where a line of convective activity fired last evening. Low-level 
flow is parallel to the upstream boundary and mid-level flow has a 
little bit more of a westerly component...such that the air mass 
will overall be moistening here in the Great Lakes (dewpoints as of 
3z are in the upper 40s to lower 50s, which is warmer than this time 
yesterday), but the most notable warm/moist advection should remain 
to our northwest near and north of Lake Superior tonight. This is 
reflected by surface warm front well to our north along the southern 
shore of Hudson Bay to western Quebec. Some moisture is swirling 
northward through the OH Valley, too, north of the aforementioned PV 
swirly in the Mid MS Valley; attm, this is slowly attempting to 
creep northward/northeastward into southern Michigan. 

PV maxima swings by to our north today, but will drag some semblance 
of a boundary across the area through the day...with NW winds 
picking up as cold advection commences late. Sunday should be 
seasonably cool with a trough axis pivoting overhead, most likely in 
the afternoon/evening. Behind this...high pressure builds in Sunday 
night, and with this cold air mass in place, think Sunday night 
could be quite cool indeed. Our quiet weather will be short-
lived...with an upper low ejecting from the PacNW across the 
northern Plains Monday...tracking across the Upper Midwest into 
southern Ontario Monday night into Tuesday. Still have concerns that 
the Gulf will be open for business with this system, and perhaps 
some tap of Pacific moisture, too, with southwesterly flow 
aloft...and thus, have concerns for heavy rain/storm potential 
across the region for this timeframe (Monday night into Tuesday). 
Progressive regime will keep this niblet moving, too, as another 
lobe of energy makes its way eastward across the central continent. 
Timing of this next feature remains a bit unclear attm, but appears 
Wednesday night into Thursday will be the broad timeframe for 
another round of activity. Even more uncertainty in the pattern for 
the end of the week into next weekend, depending on how strong the 
southern stream ridge axis will be, and where it will be focused.  

FORECAST DETAILS...

Rain/storm chances today...front crosses the region between 15-21z 
ish today from W-E and think there will be an uptick in low-level 
forcing and moisture pooling along this boundary to produce at least 
cloud cover, if not showers, especially toward the EUP and Tip of 
the Mitt where there is a likelihood of better forcing and deeper 
moisture...though instability should be lesser here (minus that 
there should be convective instability present along the edge of the 
dry slot). There is a better shot at slightly (slightly) deeper 
instability across northern Lower MI (more likely to be underneath 
the plume of weakest stability), though this will be further removed 
from the better moisture and forcing. Not impossible there could be 
a few showers or even a rumble of thunder this afternoon as the 
front passes through...but lesser moisture here signals less 
confidence in shower/storm development here. Deep layer shear picks 
up this afternoon/evening, generally in the wake of the front, but 
not impossible it could be a little better right with the front, and 
if we do end up with more activity along the front than previously 
expected...not impossible a few cells could get a little better 
organized and a little spicier. It's possible the boundary may stall 
over the region tonight, in an east-west fashion, before the next 
niblet comes rolling in for Sunday, and this idea suggests some 
shower activity will hang on into at least part of the night.  

Cool with showers Sunday; chilly Sunday night...temps will continue 
to fall Saturday night into Sunday, particularly aloft, with 850mb 
temps at or below 5C across a good chunk of the area by the
